name: Map Import & Labelling

transitions.trigger: The operator places what the drawing did not carry and links each point to what it is

notes: CF-123. **Two failure modes on one screen, kept visually apart.** Extraction is deterministic and reports which layers it found; labelling is a proposal with a confidence. **A mis-parsed layer and a bad suggestion look identical if the screen blurs them**, and the operator is left saying only that the map is wrong. **Low-confidence proposals are shown, not filtered** — the shape the assistant is unsure about is the one most worth a human looking at. **Drawn 26 August** — `Seat Board 1.dc.html` frame `seat-1a`. **The frame names this screen on its own face**, which is the first pack to do that: the earlier F&B, POS and Retail boards had to be hand-assigned by purpose after three derivation attempts produced nonsense. **A board that says what it draws removes the guess entirely.**
patternReason: the screen declares only writes (`importVenueGeometry`, `proposeVenueLabels`, `acceptVenueLabelProposals`) and no read of a population — it is settings, not a list
purpose: Upload a plan, check what was read, and review what the assistant suggests; on a map that carries bookable places, also read the cabanas, loungers and tables and join them to what they sell as (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-15 and GAP-C2).

components.label: Propose venue labels
components.notes: **Block A, bound here** (decided 29 September, AI2 review finding on BO-093). No-data AI: it reads only the shapes the import extracted, proposes, and stops; `acceptVenueLabelProposals` is the human half. When AI is off the button is hidden and the operator labels by hand on BO-094.

components.label: Accept venue label proposals
components.notes: **Accept, edit or reject, per proposal** (decided 28 September, audit R275 (f)) — each row of the review carries its own decision; an edit sends the operator's corrected point.

components.label: Propose walkways
components.notes: **A raster plan or a scanned PDF only** (the AI contract refuses a map with vector geometry, 409). On a plan with hand-marked paths it traces one segment per marked stretch (`basis: handMarked`); otherwise it proposes what it can see. Proposes and stops (3 October 2026, r1 additions, CHG-RONEC-001). Hidden when AI is off; the operator then draws paths on BO-094.

components.label: Accept or reject segment
components.notes: **One segment at a time** (Chinmay, 3 October 2026: accepted segment by segment). Each proposed segment is drawn over the plan with its confidence, low confidence shown, not hidden; Accept, Edit (move the centreline) or Reject sends one decision, and the graph validation that comes back is shown at once, so a rejected segment that strands a point says so. No accept-all.

components.label: Plan, model or navigation file
components.notes: The file being imported, uploaded before `importVenueGeometry` is called: `assets.createUpload` gives a signed URL (it refuses a GLB over 40 MB, or any file over the limit for its kind, before the transfer starts), the file goes straight to storage, and `assets.completeUpload` returns the `MediaAsset.id` sent as `sourceRef` (or `manifestRef`, `resourceManifestRef`). **The 3D model source takes two files** (ADR-0069): the GLB ("GLB, at most 40 MB; about 300,000 triangles at LOD0") as `sourceRef` and its navigation (pathway) JSON as `navigationFileRef`, each in its own slot of this upload. Needs `ASSET_LIBRARY_MANAGE` as well as `VENUE_MAP_MANAGE` (3 October 2026, CHG-RONEC-001).

components.label: Upload progress
components.notes: The transfer to storage, per file; when it ends the screen confirms it with `assets.completeUpload` and holds the `MediaAsset.id` the import takes. A file refused at `createUpload` (too large for its kind) says so before anything is sent.
Import is long enough to leave the screen. **A spinner with no proportion is a screen people reload**, and reloading an import is how a venue gets two of everything.

components.label: Format
components.notes: Required. Four source kinds (3 October 2026, r1 additions): DWG or DXF (preferred); PDF (a vector page by its layers, a scanned page through the OCR step); PNG or JPG, with or without hand-marked paths; and a 3D model (GLB) with its navigation file. SVG stays accepted. The guidance beside it says what each gives (native CAD keeps layer names; a scan gives hints and proposed paths, not geometry).

components.label: Source ref
components.notes: Required.

components.label: Read text on a scanned plan (OCR)
components.notes: `ocr.mode`, on (`auto`) by default for a scanned PDF or an image; off for a dimensioned drawing whose text is noise. The text found becomes hints for the label proposals, never labels.

components.label: Paths marked by hand, marker colour
components.notes: `handMarkedPaths`, for a PNG, JPG or scanned PDF with the walkways drawn in marker: a tick that the paths are marked, the marker colour if known (optional) and a note on what the marks mean.

components.label: Resource layer
components.notes: `layerMapping.resourceLayer`: the drawing layers that hold the bookable places (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-15). Absent, the accepted names in the venue-map input spec are matched.

components.label: Resource manifest
components.notes: `resourceManifestRef`: one sheet, header on row 3, five columns (Label, Kind, Zone, Capacity, Price band), uploaded through the asset library like the drawing. **Kind is cabana, lounger, table, pitch or other**; a table here is a non-dining spot sold like a cabana, and a restaurant table stays an F&B reservation (decided 29 September, rev 3 GAP-C2).

components.label: Price bands
components.notes: `priceBands`: each band code the manifest uses and the catalogue product variant that prices it (Family 6, Medium 10, Large 15, XL 20 on the Coastal Aqua map). **The price is the variant's**; the map holds none.

components.label: Create missing resources
components.notes: `createMissingResources`, **off by default**: where a manifest label has no resource with that code at this venue, create one instead of reporting `resourceCodeUnmatched`. Off, a mistyped label is a finding rather than a new cabana.

components.label: What the import read
components.notes: Polled while the import runs. **The resource findings are listed apart** from the geometry ones (a manifest row with no shape, a shape with no row, a label with no resource, a band with no variant), each naming the row or the label, so an operator can fix the sheet rather than guess.

components.label: What the scan, the marks and the model gave
components.notes: The text the OCR step read (with its confidence, offered to the label proposals as hints), the hand-marked strokes found, and for a GLB the measured budget line by line with the model findings and whether the 3D layer will publish (3 October 2026, CHG-RONEC-001). Each part shows only when the source had it.

components.label: Open walkway proposals
components.notes: The walkway segments `proposeWalkways` proposed and nobody has decided yet (one `ai.proposed_action` each), read again when the operator comes back to the import; each is accepted or rejected on its own with `acceptWalkwayProposals` (3 October 2026, CHG-RONEC-001).

states.error: Could not load. Names which read failed and leaves the map import labelling untouched.
states.emptyNoResults: An import that read no resources on a map meant to carry them says so (`resourcesFound` 0) and names the resource layer it looked for, rather than showing an empty price-band table.
states.emptyFirstRun: No map import labelling configured. The form opens empty and `importVenueGeometry` saves the first one; it says what the platform does in the meantime.
states.emptyNoAccess: Shown when the caller lacks `VENUE_MAP_MANAGE`, which `importVenueGeometry` requires, and names that permission. **Never an empty table** — that reads as *there is no data* and sends somebody to support with the wrong question.

name: Map Editor & Publish

transitions.trigger: A guest opens the map and is routed

notes: CF-123. **Publishing is a separate act from saving**, and the screen makes that visible — editing a live map under a guest standing in front of it is how a route ends at a wall. **Refuses to publish a point linked to a closed outlet**, naming which one: a restaurant point pointing nowhere is worse than no point, because a guest walks there. **`isStepFree` on a path is the field to get right** — a wheelchair user routed up a staircase was failed by the map, not the venue. **Graph validation runs before publish and on demand.** The screen separates two findings that read the same and are not: **an unreachable point is a defect, and a point reachable only by steps is a map that works until a wheelchair user opens it.** **Critical points — first aid, emergency exits, assembly points — are listed apart**, because an unreachable gift shop and an unreachable assembly point should not sit in one list of two hundred. **Drawn 26 August** — `Seat Board 1.dc.html` frame `seat-1b`. **The frame names this screen on its own face**, which is the first pack to do that: the earlier F&B, POS and Retail boards had to be hand-assigned by purpose after three derivation attempts produced nonsense. **A board that says what it draws removes the guess entirely.**
patternReason: `getVenueMap` reads one record and nothing reads a population — the screen is about that one thing
purpose: Place booths, toilets, exits, rides and restaurants, and the cabanas, loungers and tables guests book from the map, then publish.

components.notes: **Publishing a map moves people.** The gate names what changes before it happens — which routes, which closures, which points become unreachable.

components.label: Bookable places on the map
components.notes: **Each placed resource with its label, kind, zone, capacity and price band** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-15, superseding audit R073 (c) for resources on an ingested map). Guests pick one of these on the map and buy it. A place with no linked resource or no price band is marked, because publishing will refuse it.

components.label: What publishing changes
components.notes: **Names what goes live, where, and from when.** A publish with no stated consequence is one somebody presses meaning to save. **Lists the resource blockers apart** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-15): `resourceUnlinked` (no resource), `resourcePriceBandMissing` (no band, or a band with no variant) and `duplicateResourceLabel`, each naming the place; `validateVenueMapGraph` reports the same as resource findings before anyone presses Publish.

components.label: Place resource
components.notes: Places or amends a cabana, lounger, table (a non-dining spot; restaurant tables stay F&B reservations, rev 3 GAP-C2), pitch or other bookable place and links it to its `resources.Resource`. Bookings follow the resource, not the placement, so moving a cabana on a later version keeps its bookings.

components.label: Export navigation file
components.notes: Downloads the draft's paths and points as a navigation file (ADR-0069 section 8, closed 3 October 2026, CHG-RONEC-001), the JSON a 3D studio builds the GLB around and BO-093 imports back with the model. Codes, never ids.

components.label: Guest map artwork
components.notes: **The illustrated map guests see** (input spec section 6; the F26 brief's open item, closed 3 October 2026 here, CHG-RONEC-001): PNG or JPG up to about 12,000 px wide, uploaded through `assets.createUpload` and `completeUpload`, then set with `setVenueMapArtwork`.

components.label: Save artwork and alignment
components.notes: Sends the artwork's `baseAssetId` and two to four alignment-point pairs (a pixel on the image matched to a point on the plan; four recommended). Takes effect for guests at the next publish.

components.label: Artwork upload
components.notes: The transfer to storage; when it ends the screen confirms it with `assets.completeUpload` and holds the `MediaAsset.id` that `setVenueMapArtwork` takes.

components.label: 3D layer
components.notes: None, publishable or blocked (ADR-0069 as amended 3 October 2026). Blocked names the import job's model findings on BO-093; the 2D map still publishes and guests see 2D until a corrected model is imported.

components.label: Item description
components.notes: **What the guest reads on Item Detail** (decided 29 September, MOB-4): rides, shows, restaurants and shops. Per language.
components.provenance: agreed name venue-map VenuePoint.description (the 29 September pass brief)

components.label: Photos and video

overlays.body: **Collects what `setVenueMapArtwork` sends before it is called.** Required: `baseAssetId` (the uploaded artwork, or none to remove it) and, with an image, `baseImageAlignment`: the image size and two to four alignment pairs, each a point clicked on the artwork and the same point clicked on the plan. Dismissing sends nothing; the map keeps the artwork it had.

**Collects what `setVenuePoint` sends before it is called.** Required: `kind`, `name`, `position`. Optional: `nameLocalised`, `outletId`, `productId`, `accessPointId`, `isStepFree`, `openingHours`, `iconRef`, `isActive`, `isNavigable`, `isDestination`, `pointId`; and the item details decided 29 September (MOB-4, MOB-6): `description`, `media`, `featuredOffer` (a product or a bundle, on any kind of point), `typicalDurationMinutes`, `interestTags`, `cuisineTags`; and `retailTags` (30 September, MoM 4.7). Dismissing sends nothing; the screen behind is unchanged. Not asked, because the server sets them (readOnly in the contract): `id`, `mapId` (3 October 2026, CHG-SPF-001).
**Collects what `publishVenueMap` sends before it is called.** Nothing in the body is required. Optional: `note`. Dismissing sends nothing; the screen behind is unchanged.

**Collects what `setPathClosure` sends before it is called.** Required: `isClosed`. Optional: `reason` (maintenance, incident, event, weather, crowding, other), `note`, `force`, `expectedReopenAt`. **Choosing Other makes the note required** — the form will not confirm without it and the server refuses 400 (decided 28 September, audit R222). Dismissing sends nothing; the screen behind is unchanged.

**Collects what `setPlacedResource` sends before it is called.** `resourceId` (the resource it is), `label` (what the guest taps, e.g. B09; unique on the map), `kind` (cabana, lounger, table, pitch, other), `zone`, `capacity` (1 to 500, checked against the party at hold), `priceBandCode` (one of the bands given at import; its variant prices it), `position` or `boundary`, `isBookable`; `placedResourceId` to amend one. Decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-15. Dismissing sends nothing; the screen behind is unchanged.
